item.title: Bridges & Brunch with Strasburg Scooter Tours — Sat Oct 3 — Strasburg Scooter Tours
item.description:
Experience a relaxing morning ride through the back roads of Amish Country in Lancaster County, PA. Along the way to a 19th century covered bridge, enjoy the scenery of rolling hills, breathtaking views, and our Amish neighbors going about their daily routines. A guided tour of one of Lancaster County’s most beautiful covered bridges An opportunity for a close up of daily life in Amish Country $10 dining voucher to one of two of Strasburg’s favorites brunch spots, Casey Jones’ Restaurant and Speckled Hen*
And each trip is unique, so you never know what we might have in store for you! *Unfortunately, we regret to inform you that some of the food offerings on the tour may not be considered ‘Kosher.’ We apologize for any inconvenience.

item.title: Spooky Scoot Tour with Strasburg Scooter Tours — Sat Oct 3 — Strasburg Scooter Tours
item.description:

Follow your guide deep into the night in one of our two-person Scoot Coupes as they lead you on a hair-raising adventure, traveling along eerie back roads, zipping past the pumpkin patch, making stops to hear local folklore and the lesser-known haunted side of Lancaster County. item.title: Lancaster Breakfast and History Walking Tour — Sat Oct 3, 9:00 AM — Unique Lancaster
item.description:
Searching for a walking history tour in Lancaster? You’re in for a flavorful experience—literally!
Introducing the Lancaster History & Breakfast Walking Tour—a dynamic two-hour adventure that blends the rich heritage of one of America’s oldest inland cities with a delicious morning meal. Explore Lancaster’s vibrant streets with a professionally trained local guide and journey through time from the early 1700s through the transformative decades of the 20th century.
Brought to you by Unique Lancaster Experiences, this guided walk kicks off with your choice of hot or iced coffee or tea to energize your morning. Along the way, you’ll hear engaging stories about Lancaster’s evolution as a bustling Market City and its transition from trolleys to automobiles after WWI.
But this isn’t your standard history tour. You’ll dive into interactive discussions and uncover captivating insights about colonial life, architectural landmarks, and the impact of prohibition on the region.

item.description:

As we look toward the future, the Lititz Art Association is excited to announce some major updates for the 2026 showcase! A Shift to Autumn: We are moving from the heat of late July to the crisp, inspiring air of Fall.
A New Setting: While we’ve loved our time in the park, this year’s show will move to a new location to better accommodate our growing community of art lovers.
Moravian Church Square – 8 Church Square, Lititz Date: Saturday, October 3rd Time: 9AM – 5PM

item.title: Screen Printing Social Justice Posters Workshop at PCA&D — Wed Oct 7, 6:00 PM — Pennsylvania College of Art & Design – Center for Creative Exploration
item.description:
Printed media has a long history of being used as a tool in activism and social justice movements. Printmaking allows one to make multiple copies of their artwork, ideas, and beliefs and distribute them to friends, on the street, and anywhere else they can think of. In this class, students will create a poster design for a subject they feel passionate about and bring it to life as a screen printed poster. This class will cover a brief history of social justice posters, the process of creating a screen, and screenprinting techniques. At the end of the class, students are free to trade copies of their posters with each other. All supplies will be provided. Just bring your ideas!
Register Now

item.description: With Father David Peck and Professor Randall Zachman Entirely on Zoom Now in its seventh year, the 2026 Mercy Seminar invites you to explore the profound insights that different faith traditions offer about embracing life and navigating death with grace. How can the certainty of death inspire us to cultivate a deeper focus and a heart full of gratitude, transforming potential feelings of anxiety into a courageous appreciation for the present moment? Is death merely “nothing at all,” or does it open the gateway to an eternal adventure beyond this life? Join us as we delve into selected sacred readings from Hindu, Buddhist, Jewish, Christian, and Muslim scriptures, along with enlightening contemporary secular spiritual writings. Together, we will uncover the wisdom that encourages us to live our best lives and face death not with fear, but with hope and understanding. item.title: Evening Compline — Thu Oct 8, 9:00 PM — Saint James Episcopal Church
item.description:
Evening Compline via Zoom Click here to join Compline. (This link can be used for every evening Compline on Zoom.)
The short service of Compline is based on the closing time of prayer in the Daily Office, or monastic cycle of prayer. It is observed in monasteries around 8 or 9 PM when darkness has fallen and bedtime is near.
The thoughts that inspire the prayers during Compline are the need for divine forgiveness and protection against the powers of darkness. Prayers for peace and rest are offered as night falls.
People of all faiths and beliefs are invited to this contemplative service. The service lasts about 20 minutes.
Source: Saint James Lancaster

item.title: What Teeth Tell Us — Sat Oct 3, 11:00 AM — Lancaster
item.description:
Presentation, Everyone
What big teeth you have!Most dinosaurs are known for their incredible teeth! By studying their teeth alone, scientists can decide what each type ate for dinner whether it be meat, plants, or a little bit of everything. In modern times we still use the teeth in animals’ skulls to learn a lot about them. Join a Naturalist from Lancaster County's Department of Parks & Recreation to discover the science of teeth and what they can tell us. Then, try your hand at identifying skulls to figure out what certain mystery animals like to have for dinner. All ages · Walk-ins welcome

item.title: Evening Compline — Wed Oct 7, 9:00 PM — Saint James Episcopal Church
item.description:
Evening Compline via Zoom Click here to join Compline. (This link can be used for every evening Compline on Zoom.)
The short service of Compline is based on the closing time of prayer in the Daily Office, or monastic cycle of prayer. It is observed in monasteries around 8 or 9 PM when darkness has fallen and bedtime is near.
The thoughts that inspire the prayers during Compline are the need for divine forgiveness and protection against the powers of darkness. Prayers for peace and rest are offered as night falls.
People of all faiths and beliefs are invited to this contemplative service. The service lasts about 20 minutes.
